rationale: A wins because it treats the missing stablecoin, partner, market list, customer, and cost data as gating facts, not decoration. Its line “Named stablecoin and settlement partner (critical — a story about replacing correspondent banking needs to show what it is being replaced with)” is the adult in the room. B has the same basic four angles, but it lets phrasing like “One of the biggest cross-border payment networks is now settling in stablecoins” outrun the source material. That is how a decent angle becomes a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: “£30B stablecoin bet lands” overstates the supplied fact. Wise moves over £30B per quarter overall; the update does not say £30B will settle through stablecoins.

“a company routing £30B per quarter removes their cut” implies correspondent banks lose the whole Wise volume. The angle needs to say potential pressure, not pretend the migration has already happened.
“EU MiCA, U.S. stablecoin bills, UK FCA regime, Asian frameworks” is useful context, but none of those regimes are named in the update. Keep them as questions, not implied facts.
“The stablecoin boring-infrastructure moment” is clever-desk phrasing. Fine for internal strategy, too cute for an actual pitch subject line.
gaps_in_B: “One of the biggest cross-border payment networks” is not proved by the update. £30B per quarter shows scale; it does not establish rank.
“settling in stablecoins” plural is sloppy. The update says a regulated stablecoin, and the specific stablecoin is unnamed.
“confirmation of the specific stablecoin and regulatory partner” invents a regulatory partner. The update says the stablecoin and partner are unnamed; it does not say the partner is regulatory.

“a live map of which regulators are ready for crypto settlement” overclaims. A region-by-region rollout may reflect regulatory readiness, product sequencing, risk appetite, or commercial priorities. Reporters will not let that slide.
